answers.q1: 'round' → 'halfExpand'; 'floor' → 'expand' if negative, else 'trunc'; 'ceil' → 'trunc' if negative, else 'expand'; anything else (undefined) → undefined.
answers.q2: It accepts undefined or one of 'round', 'floor', 'ceil' (via the ROUNDING_MODES set); any other value throws a TypeError saying "Expected roundingMode to be one of 'round', 'floor' or 'ceil'".
answers.q3: With fraction-digit options the existing code truncates (1999 with maximumFractionDigits:1 gives '1.9 kB'), while the 3-significant-digit default rounds, so 'round' can't be both default and current behaviour. The agent left the default undefined: omitted keeps the old output exactly (rounds without fraction options, truncates with them), and explicit 'round' rounds; this is documented in readme.md.
answers.q4: If the mode isn't 'trunc' and the exponent isn't the last unit, it formats the value with the same options via toLocaleString and, if the rounded result is >= base, divides number by base and increments exponent, so 999_960 becomes '1 MB'.
answers.q5: Without fraction-digit options 'round' keeps using Number#toPrecision, which depends on the floating-point representation of 1.005, giving '1 kB'. With fraction-digit options it goes through Intl.NumberFormat, which rounds the shortest decimal form 1.005, so it gives '1.01 kB'.
answers.q6: It uses exact bigint arithmetic: multiplies by 10^maximumFractionDigits, divides by the scale, and adds 1 to the digits if mode is 'expand' with a nonzero remainder, or 'halfExpand' with remainder*2 >= scale; trunc leaves it, then it splits whole and fraction.
answers.q7: It checks that floor of -value equals '-' plus ceil of value, for values [1, 1001, 1337, 1999, 54321, 999901] and maximumFractionDigits of [undefined, 0, 1, 2].
answers.q8: The 'rounding up carries onto the next unit' test failed because it expected '999.960 kB' but got '999.96 kB' (minimumFractionDigits:1 only sets a minimum). The agent fixed the test expectation to '999.96 kB'.
answers.q9: It created a throwaway fake 'ava' module (node:test/assert wrappers) in the scratchpad's node_modules, copied index.js and test.js there, and ran node --test test.js. It first broke because the shim lacked test.skip (and notRegex), after the first heredoc attempt was also blocked by the tool's brace/quote check.
answers.q10: 'documented examples are accurate' still failed because the shim directory had no readme.md or index.d.ts to read. After copying those in, the suite gave 48 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped (already test.skip), and test-rounding.js passed 11/11.
